item.title: Aylore Hari Suryanarayana Wins RCA below 1800 Classical Rating 2026
item.description: Aylore Hari Suryanarayana scored an unbeaten 8/9 points to win the RCA below 1800 Classical Rating Chess Tournament 2026. Aylore Hari, Siddharth Pernati, and Johney Mandal all scored 8/9 points to finish in the top 3 places according to tiebreak scores. The tournament was organised at the Hall of Chess, Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Chennai, from 17th to 19th July 2026 by Rajam Chess Academy. The total prize fund was ₹2,00,000, with top 3 prizes of ₹25,000, ₹15,000 and ₹12,500 along with trophies. Photos: WFM M.R. Sangeetha

item.title: 2nd MCF GM/IM Invitational 2026: Photo Story from Kuala Lumpur
item.description: Last year, the inaugural GM/IM Invitation Chess Event wrote itself into Malaysian chess history. It was at that historic tournament where then-IM Yeoh Li Tian achieved his third and final GM norm, officially becoming Malaysia’s first-ever Grandmaster. Fast forward to 2026, and the search for Malaysia's next Grandmaster and International Master continues! The 2nd GM-IM Invitational Chess Championship 2026 is currently underway from 29th July to 6th August 2026 at the scenic Jeumpa d'Ramo Boutique Hotel in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Photos: Edwin Lam

item.title: Sipke Ernst: The Modern Benko Gambit | A Complete Repertoire for Black
item.description: In modern chess, activity has become one of the most prized resources of all. Engines have taught us again and again that active piece play, the initiative, and dynamic pressure can more than compensate for small material or structural concessions. The Benko Gambit fits this philosophy perfectly. By giving up a pawn early, Black immediately gets exactly what the modern player is looking for: open lines, harmonious development, and relentless, long-term pressure on White's queenside.Click Hereto Buy!

item.title: Pune Chess Hangouts Finds a Saturday Home at The Habitat
item.description: Pune’s chess scene just levelled up! Pune Chess Hangouts is launching a brand-new weekly fixture: a dedicated Saturday Chess Club at The Habitat in Mundhwa, running every weekend from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM. This gives the city its very first consistent Saturday evening hub for chess enthusiasts. Founded in early 2024 by Sanjana Desai and Chaitanya Bidkar, Pune Chess Hangouts started as a modest gathering of a few players. Under Sanjana’s leadership as Founder and Community Head, it has rapidly expanded into one of the city's most vibrant chess hubs, boasting over 1,000 members and a track record of more than 250 weekend meetups across Pune.

item.title: Double Gold for India! Harika Dronavalli Dominates Asian Women's Rapid & Blitz Championships 2026
item.description: Indian Legend Harika Dronavalli clinched double gold at the Asian Women's Rapid & Blitz Championships 2026. Harika scored 8.5/11 points to win the Rapid, remaining unbeaten throughout the event. In Blitz, she scored 10.5/13 points to clinch Gold. Her historic double-gold performance brought home two trophies and a total cash prize of 33,000 HKD. The Tournament was organised from 28th to 30th July at the TWGHs Tungpo Kitty Woo Stadium in Kowloon, Hong Kong.

item.title: 2nd Sahel Chess Festival 2026: Tunisian Coastal City of Monastir Set to Host an Exciting Chess Festival
item.description: Following the remarkable success of its inaugural edition, the Sahel Chess Festival is back for its second edition, scheduled to take place from October 24 to November 1, 2026, in the beautiful coastal city of Monastir, Tunisia. Designed to bring together chess enthusiasts from around the globe, this international event combines high-level competitive play with a wonderful week of cultural exchange and leisure.

item.title: FIDE Rating list August 2026: Arjun and Humpy in World Top 10
item.description: The August 2026 FIDE rating list sees Arjun Erigaisi and Koneru Humpy as India’s only representatives in the World Top 10. India has 14 players in the Open Top 100 and ten in the Women’s Top 100, with several notable rating changes following tournaments in July. Praggnanandhaa, Aravindh Chithambaram, Raunak Sadhwani and Savitha Shri made significant gains in the rapid and blitz formats. India also retained the World No. 2 position among the top federations in the Open, Women’s and Mixed categories.

item.title: IMC India donates Rs. 5,00,000 to support Aarit Kapil's journey to the IM title
item.description: In recent times, there has been a surge in corporate interest in promoting chess. Many companies now align with our mission to support talented players who are facing financial hurdles on their path to the top. Continuing this welcome trend, IMC India has once again stepped forward, this time donating Rs. 5,00,000 to the HelpChess Foundation. This scholarship amount will be given to 10-year-old Aarit Kapil from New Delhi to support his pursuit of the IM title.

item.title: Aswin P.G. Dominates at 40th RCC Below 1800 Rapid Rating 2026
item.description: Aswin P.G. scored an unbeaten 8.5/9 to win the 40th RCC Rapid Chess Tournament for Below 1800. Aswin scored 8 consecutive victories and drew his final round to win the tournament. Prakyath G and Rithesh K scored 8/9 to secure 2nd and 3rd places according to tiebreak scores. Rao's Chess Corner organised this tournament at Achuthpal Hall in Mangalore from 25th to 26th July 2026. The total prize fund was ₹50,000, with top 3 prizes of ₹17,000, ₹10,000, and ₹5,000 along with trophies. Photos: Rao's Chess Corner

item.title: Kevilekho Zumvu Becomes 22nd Nagaland Classical State Champion 2026
item.description: Kevilekho Zumvu scored an unbeaten 7/8 points to win the 22nd Nagaland State FIDE Rating Chess Championship 2026. Salhuto Nyekha, Khrielie Sano, and Melesai scored 6.5/8 to finish in 2nd to 4th places according to tiebreak scores. The top 4 players will represent Nagaland in the upcoming National Championship. The tournament was organised from 16th to 18th July 2026 in Kohima, Nagaland. Photos: Mr.Mengise Haikam

item.title: Bodhana Sivanandan breaks the record!
item.description: An eleven-year-old British chess player has become the youngest girl to defeat a grandmaster rated above 2600, breaking a 38-year-old record previously held by Hungarian all-time great Judit Polgar. Bodhana Sivanandan defeated a French grandmaster rated 2628, and the international news media went wild over this extraordinary feat. Bodhana is a special member of the ChessBase family and will most likely play in the Hamburg Bundesliga team.

item.title: Nihal Shetty Wins RCC Khannur Below 1800 Classical Rating 2026
item.description: Nihal N Shetty scored an unbeaten 8/9 points to win the RCC Khannur Below 1800 Classical Rating Chess Tournament 2026. Nihal Shetty and Supriyo Das both scored 8/9 points, but a better tiebreak score helped Nihal clinch the title, and Supriyo finished in 2nd place. Rao's Chess Corner organised this tournament at Achuthpal Hall, Mangalore, from 24th to 26th July 2026. The total prize fund was ₹5,00,000, with top 3 prizes of ₹60,000, ₹40,000, and ₹30,000 along with trophies. Photos: Rao's Chess Corner

item.title: Team USA Defeats Team Uzbekistan 14-10 to Claim WR Chess Miami Title
item.description: The WR Chess Masters in Miami, Florida, concluded with an exciting battle between two major forces in world chess: Team USA and Team Uzbekistan. Organized by WR Chess, the event featured five top Grandmasters from the United States competing against five leading players from Uzbekistan across Rapid and Blitz formats. Playing in a 4-board Scheveningen format across two days (4 rounds of Rapid and 8 rounds of Blitz), every round victory was worth 2 match points, a tie worth 1 point, and a loss 0 points. Photos: Abhyudaya Ram

item.title: Maurice Ashley Chess Fellowship Empowers Rising Talent
item.description: The Maurice Ashley Chess Fellowship, established by history-making Grandmaster Maurice Ashley in partnership with the U.S. Chess Trust, continues its mission to support young, talented chess players from underrepresented backgrounds and help them pursue professional careers in chess. Seven promising young players will receive a combined $31,000 to support tournament participation, coaching, supplies, and other essential expenses as they continue their development and pursue their goals at the highest levels of competitive chess.
